analysis.original_request: Design an isotropic all-dielectric planar multilayer polarizing beam splitter on a fused-silica substrate for incidence from air at 45 degrees. Across 500-650 nm, favor high TE reflectance and high TM transmittance. Use only MgF2, SiO2, Ta2O5, and TiO2; compare structures with 6, 10, and 14 finite layers, with each layer constrained to 25-220 nm. Treat mean TE reflectance of at least 90% and mean TM transmittance of at least 85% as soft goals, while also rewarding fewer layers and lower total thickness. Report the best-performance, most-robust, and simplest candidates rather than imposing a hard feasibility threshold. Evaluate numerical manufacturing sensitivity using independent normally distributed layer-thickness errors with a standard deviation of 1.5% of each nominal thickness and a common incidence-angle offset bounded by plus or minus 1 degree.
analysis.normalized_request_english: Design and optimize isotropic all-dielectric planar multilayer polarizing beam splitters on a fused-silica substrate with incidence from air at 45 degrees across the 500-650 nm wavelength band. The design must utilize materials selected from MgF2, SiO2, Ta2O5, and TiO2. Compare configurations with exactly 6, 10, and 14 layers, where each layer thickness is constrained between 25 nm and 220 nm. Optimize for high TE reflectance (mean >= 90%) and high TM transmittance (mean >= 85%) as soft scoring preferences, while simultaneously penalizing layer count and total physical thickness. Identify candidates that offer the best performance, highest robustness, and simplest structure The numerical performance targets are soft scoring preferences. Perform robustness analysis by evaluating sensitivity to independent normally distributed layer-thickness errors (sigma = 1.5% of nominal thickness) and a common incidence-angle uncertainty bounded by +/- 1 degree.
analysis.compatibility_reason: The request specifies planar, laterally uniform, linear, isotropic layered media under frequency-domain plane-wave illumination. It involves standard dielectric materials and does not require gratings, metasurfaces, anisotropy, chirality, magnetism, nonlinearity, near-field calculations, or time-domain simulations.
known_stack_materials: available coating materials: MgF2, SiO2, Ta2O5, TiO2
manufacturing_constraints: layer thicknesses bounded between 25 nm and 220 nm
total layer counts restricted to 6, 10, or 14
ambiguities: specific ordering of materials within the stack is not fixed and must be determined by optimization
exact definition of 'simplest' beyond layer count and thickness is not specified, though layer count and total thickness are explicitly rewarded
method_research_questions: How to effectively combine performance metrics (TE R, TM T) with complexity penalties (layer count, total thickness) into a single scalar objective function for multi-objective optimization?
What is the optimal strategy for sampling the discrete material choices combined with continuous thickness variables within the specified constraints?
